correctness.rationale: Checked representation of selected tuples by a first independent subsequence of nonzero singular vectors, Gram pairing matrix and coordinate words. Witt extension makes equal state tuples lie in the same orthogonal orbit. Gaussian Fourier inversion gives exact number of singular extension vectors with prescribed pairings t: 2^{-m-1}(2^{2r}+epsilon*2^r Σ_a(-1)^{q_W(a)+a·t}), subtracting in-span/zero. For m<=3, at r>=5 the lower bound 2^{2r-m-1}-2^{r-1}>2^m ensures every out-of-span pairing pattern exists, so four-round EF types stabilize. Independently implemented the complete one-point-extension state recursion and compared exact rank3/4 fingerprints for all signs r=2..5: rank3 groups are {(2,-)} and remainder; rank4 groups {(2,-)}, {(2,+)}, {(3,-)}, remainder. Separately enumerated explicit finite singular-point adjacency to check E/claw/K4 patterns through r=4, confirming 5/9/27/35 sharp representatives. These finite boundary checks plus analytic uniform-extension bound prove the all-r statement, assuming Witt extension and the displayed standard Gauss identity. No higher quantifier depth or larger fields claimed.

value.rationale: The exact rank-four logical equivalence classes of a natural parameterized finite polar-geometry graph family are substantive descriptive-complexity information. They give a sharp small-representative bound, explicit low-depth separators and an infinite stabilization theorem, not merely tiny graph enumeration. The projective singular locus in F2 differs from symplectic all-point graphs, motivating this precise classification.

final_claim: The binary orthogonal polar singular-point graphs Γ(r,epsilon), r>=2, partition into exactly four elementary-equivalence classes at quantifier rank four: singleton (2,-) on 5 points, (2,+) on 9, (3,-) on 27, and every remaining model with smallest representative (3,+) on 35; quantifier rank 3 has two classes. E, induced claw, and 4-clique distinguish all four classes; 35 is the sharp family-representative bound.
limitations: Only finite nondegenerate even-dimensional F2 quadratic forms, singular nonzero points, adjacency/equality language, and rank<=4.
Analytic extension guarantee for r>=5, small finite enumeration for r=2..4; no promise of higher-depth classification or arbitrary q.
